items.title: A bounded-above complex of finite stably free modules lifts along an ideal of invertible elements
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, a complex E^bullet of R/I-modules and an object K of D(R), under four hypotheses: E^bullet is a bounded above complex of finite stably free R/I-modules; K tensor^L_R R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I); K^bullet is pseudo-coherent; and every element of 1 + I is invertible. It concludes that there is a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite stably free R-modules representing K in D(R) with P^bullet tensor_R R/I isomorphic to E^bullet, and moreover that P^i is free wherever E^i is (source lines 19516-19530). The proof is structurally parallel to the projective case: it applies the abstract lifting lemma for complexes with respect to the class of all finite stably free R-modules (proof lines 19532-19534). Property (1) is immediate; property (2) follows from the exact category statement for stably free modules; property (3) follows from Nakayama's lemma; property (4) follows from the liftability of finite stably free modules along an ideal consisting of elements of 1 + I; and part (5) holds because a pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules (proof lines 19534-19542). The final assertion follows from the statement on isomorphism classes of finite projective lifts (proof lines 19543-19544). The non-routine content is the verification of the eigenvalue-type hypothesis, namely that the stably free class is well behaved under the given condition on 1 + I, which is what makes property (2) and property (4) available.
